summaries.demographer: John Marquette is a 57-year-old White, non-Hispanic married man living in Benson, North Carolina, with his wife Diane (Q51, Q84, Q88, Q89). He was born and raised in Angier, North Carolina, in a working-class two-parent household with one sister, and both parents completed high school (Q87, Q97-Q101). He has an associate degree, is enrolled part time online toward a bachelor's degree, and works full time as a courier/messenger while his wife works part time at a dental office (Q16, Q74, Q90-Q92). His children are grown, and his life course is now shaped by grandparenthood, aging-parent support, mortgage stability, and late-career advancement goals (Q05, Q35, Q58, Q108).
summaries.behavioral_economist: John is a planner with strong loss aversion around money, time, and reliability; he tracks spending, plans routes, and budgets using spreadsheets and notebooks (Q03, Q57, Q65). He responds to uncertainty by making systems, such as medication charts for his mother or route plans for work (Q44, Q65). His incentives are identity-based as much as financial: supervisory advancement, mentoring, and efficient eco-friendly delivery appeal because they validate his competence and usefulness (Q16, Q65, Q108). He is cautious with debt, can absorb a $400 emergency, and cuts discretionary spending before risking late bills (Q60-Q64, Q82).
summaries.political_scientist: John is a regular voter who prioritizes local governance, roads, schools, growth planning, and institutional competence (Q23, Q24). He identifies as a moderate Republican or conservative-leaning independent, closer to the Republican Party but not strongly partisan, and is willing to cross party lines locally (Q95, Q96). His politics combine fiscal caution and work-centered conservatism with pragmatic support for infrastructure, public institutions, clean transportation, and some environmental investment (Q24, Q25). On race and policing, he is reflective and moderately affected by Black Lives Matter, influenced by coworkers, museum history work, and family discussions rather than protest participation (Q26-Q30).
summaries.psychologist: John presents as conscientious, orderly, dependable, and mildly anxious when plans break down; he copes by making lists, walking, painting, listening to jazz, and talking with Diane (Q03, Q43-Q45, Q50). His self-concept is rooted in usefulness, competence, family duty, and keeping one's word (Q01, Q65, Q109). He is intellectually curious and imaginative, using photography, watercolor, speculative fiction, philosophy, and local history to expand beyond his traditional upbringing (Q07, Q15, Q17, Q47). Relationally, he is steady rather than demonstrative, showing care through errands, repairs, calls, meals, mentoring, and practical presence (Q05-Q07, Q35, Q46, Q109).
